title: WhatsApp: unread badge can exceed the phone count for chats without an app-state markChatAsRead entry
description: Per-chat unread is reconciled from (a) history-sync UnreadCount, (b) on-demand history ingested read, (c) app-state markChatAsRead last-read cutoff. A chat with genuine unread but no markChatAsRead entry and no fresh history sync keeps every locally ingested historical message as unread (observed group with 235 unread locally; phone count unknown). Needs an authoritative per-chat unread source or a history resync trigger. Desired outcome: reconcile unread to an authoritative per-chat count or trigger a history resync so historical messages without a markChatAsRead entry do not inflate the unread badge. Files/functions: megachatd/internal/proto/whatsapp/history.go (reconcileChatUnread), events.go, appstate.go.
notes:
worker: root cause — unread reconciliation only ran while a phone signal was being applied: ingestConversation used the sync's UnreadCount once then discarded it, and a message-less conversation returned early before reconciling, dropping the count; FetchHistory/startup resync only ask the phone when the cache is sparse, so a chat with a full local cache and no markChatAsRead entry (WhatsApp compacts old read mutations) had no heal path — hence 235 bogus unread. Fix: record the phone's count with its boundary (chatMeta.UnreadTS/UnreadKnown), apply it for message-less conversations too, mark read only what an on-demand page actually delivered (pageTS, so newer genuine unread survives), fold store per-key unread per chat (new Store.UnreadCounts) and re-apply snapshots where local unread exceeds the phone's count, and — for chats with unread and no trusted count — request that chat's history from the phone once per chat per process (the bead's resync trigger). files: megachatd/internal/proto/whatsapp/{backend.go,history.go,send.go,history_test.go,helpers_test.go}. tests added: TestHistorySyncMessageLessConversationAppliesUnreadCount, TestReconcileUnreadAsksThePhoneForChatsWithoutASnapshot, TestOnDemandHistoryKeepsTheNewerUnread, TestUnreadSnapshotIsReappliedToLateHistory, TestUnreadHealAsksAndAppliesThePhoneCount (each verified failing with its part of the fix disabled). gates: go vet ok; go test -race ok (whatsapp re-run -count=1 12.3s, new tests pass individually); contract 589 passed/0 failed; pytest skipped: no python changed. follow-ups: freshest count is still bounded by the last history sync (whatsmeow exposes no unread API); a phone that never answers a heal request is retried only on the next process start.
rework: Approved: root cause, UnreadTS/UnreadKnown boundary, message-less conversations, pageTS, Store.UnreadCounts folding, applyUnreadSnapshots (only ever marks read), and the 5 tests. Fix these in askUntrustedUnread (the new phone requests): (1) It fires one on-demand history request per chat for EVERY chat with unread and no snapshot, back to back, at startup. Bulk peer requests to the phone risk WhatsApp rate limiting; Python never did this. Bound and pace it: at most 10 chats per process, highest local unread first, at least 5 s between requests, and keep the existing per-chat historyAskCooldown. Make the cap and spacing constants with a test. (2) The goroutine uses context.Background(): use the backend's lifecycle context so Disconnect/Stop cancels pending asks, and test that Stop ends it promptly. (3) Evidence: requestOlderHistory asks for OLDER messages anchored on the oldest cached one. Show from whatsmeow (proto/waHistorySync, the ON_DEMAND response handling) that this response carries Conversation.UnreadCount for the chat. If it does not reliably, say so in the report and in megachatd/README.md (best-effort heal), and keep the snapshot re-apply as the primary mechanism. (4) Nit: the heal helpers live in send.go; move them to history.go next to reconcileChatUnread. Final gates as per AGENTS.md: go test -race ./... once at the end, full result in the note.
close_reason: Controller reviewed: snapshot re-apply primary; phone asks capped 10/process, 5s spacing, cancelled on Disconnect; worker gates: race 19/19 ok, contract 589/589

title: WhatsApp: archived chats without local history disappear from the chat list after restart
description: The chat registry is rebuilt from message cache/contacts on start; whatsmeow_chat_settings holds archived rows for chats with no local messages (observed: 0@s.whatsapp.net, 157968947515605@lid, 176282805522608@lid, 214340544290860@lid, 393472482603@c.us), so after a restart only the archived chats with messages show. Proposed: seed the registry from whatsmeow_chat_settings (enumerate via b.db, like lidBulkImport does with whatsmeow_lid_map) in syncArchiveFlags/loadContacts, naming via nameForChat/+phone fallback. Desired outcome: archived chats without local history remain in the chat list after restart. Files/functions: megachatd/internal/proto/whatsapp/appstate.go (syncArchiveFlags), contacts.go (loadContacts).
notes: rework: seedArchivedChats reads 'SELECT chat_jid FROM whatsmeow_chat_settings WHERE archived' for ALL accounts. The table's key is (our_jid, chat_jid) and whatsmeow's own ChatSettings lookups always filter by the current device; rows from a previous pairing or another account in the same whatsmeow.db would leak into the chat list. Scope it: WHERE our_jid = ? AND archived, with the current device JID in the same form whatsmeow stores it (check store/sqlstore: it uses the non-AD own JID, i.e. client.Store.ID.ToNonAD().String()); return early when not paired. Add a test with rows for two our_jid values asserting only the current account's archived chats are seeded. Everything else is approved (root cause, noteChat naming fallback, no duplicates, broadcast skip, both tests).
close_reason: Controller verified: go vet/test -race, 589 contract; seed scoped to device JID (whatsmeow stores jid.String())
